materials.title: Subtitle Tone Choice
materials.text:
A short subtitle can look straightforward until two translators disagree about the tone of the same line. One hears a joke; the other hears a complaint. The words alone may not settle the matter, particularly when the actor's expression is partly hidden ____1____ view.

A film club comparing two translations began by watching the whole exchange instead of isolating the sentence. What came before and after it made a difference ____2____ how the line could be understood. A reply might reveal that the previous speaker had been teasing, or that a joke had not been received as intended.

Even with that context, more than one translation could remain defensible. The club learned to ask what each version emphasised and what it left ____3____. Brevity required choices, and those choices could affect the impression of a relationship between characters.

This was not a reason to say that accuracy did not matter. ____4____ the contrary, it made a precise account of the disagreement more important. The question was not simply which translator was right, but which features of the exchange each had tried to preserve.

The discussion also changed how members watched the film. They became alert ____5____ pauses and gestures they had previously passed over. A subtitle was one part of an encounter, not the whole of it.

By the end, the group had not produced a single perfect sentence. It had gained a clearer sense of what a translation was responsible ____6____. A short line could be judged in relation ____7____ the scene and its constraints, rather ____8____ against an imagined version that lost nothing and needed no space.

questions.explanation: hidden from view固定不见，of不合。
make a difference to固定影响理解。
leave out或leave unsaid都可表达未呈现，into不合。
On the contrary固定相反，In不合。
alert to固定留意。
responsible for固定负责。
in relation to固定相关。
rather than固定对照。

units.title: 高级填空：修好工具之后的熟练程度

materials.title: Restored Tool Skill
materials.text:
When a hand tool returned from repair, a workshop volunteer described it as “ready to use”. A new member understood this to mean that anyone could use it successfully. The tool had been checked, but the phrase said nothing ____1____ the user's experience.

The workshop revised its return notes to keep those questions separate. A serviceable object and a skilled user were not the same thing. The condition of the tool could be recorded, while an offer of instruction made clear where a beginner could ask ____2____ help.

One experienced member thought the distinction was obvious. It was obvious to him because he had already learned what the tool required. The phrase had been read in the light ____3____ knowledge that a newcomer did not necessarily possess.

The revised note did not need to include a complete manual. It needed to avoid giving the impression that the repair had brought every possible uncertainty to ____4____ end. A short reference to the workshop's induction session was enough to point towards the next step.

The group tested the wording with someone who had not used the equipment before. ____5____ sooner had she read it than she asked where to book the session. That question suggested the note was doing something useful: it connected a statement about the object with a route to learning about its use.

The workshop kept the old wording as an example, not as a person to blame. It showed how a sentence could be correct within one understanding and misleading ____6____ another. The answer lay not in abandoning brief language ____7____ in making a crucial boundary visible. A repair could restore a tool ____8____ it could not supply the experience of the person holding it.

questions.explanation: say nothing about/of userexperience均可，at不合。
ask for help固定求助，to help在该名词后位置不合。
in the light of固定根据，to不合。
bring...to an end固定，end元音前an。
No sooner...than固定倒装，Not sooner不引同结构。
under/within/in another understanding均可表达另一理解框架，不以介词差别误拒；by another不表该所在框架。
not in X but in Y对照，or不完成该肯定替代结构。
工具能修复但不提供经验，but/yet/though引转折或让步；so误成修复故不能供经验的因果。
